A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ESR spectra of Na_{2}(Rb, Cs)C_{60} polymers are dominated by the presence of a small amount of the single bonded phase.
the polymerized phases of Na_{2}(Rb,Cs)C_{60} are not quasi- one dimensional.

the PP of Na_2CsC_{60}, Na_2RbC_{60}, and Na_2CsRbC_{6} are AF metals with a small AF spin gap, and that the PP of the Na_2Rbc_{60} (r=0.3,0.4,0.5,0.7) are inhomogeneous, with a large fraction of the material in the metallic state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ESR studies of PP are complicated by the fact that the samples are inhomogeneous and that the spin species detected by ESR can be of different origin.
the ESR spectra of the polymer phase are dominated by the nonpolymerized phase, and that the ESR data of Arcon et al., as presented, cannot be used as evidence for low dimensional instabilities.
the PP of Na2CsC60 is not a good candidate to look for a novel ground state in fullerides.
